meaning: An accessory is part of the installation that supports, connects or controls electrical equipment or wiring, but is not itself classed as current-using equipment.
studyNote: Think of it as an installation device that serves the wiring or the equipment rather than converting electrical energy into light, heat or motion.
distinction: Do not confuse an accessory with an appliance or other current-using equipment.

meaning: Ambient temperature is the temperature of the air or other surrounding medium in the place where equipment operates.
studyNote: It matters because electrical equipment and conductors are selected and rated for stated environmental conditions; a hotter or colder surrounding environment can affect suitability.

meaning: An appliance is a type of current-using equipment, but in this historical definition it excludes luminaires and independent motors.
studyNote: The term identifies equipment whose purpose is to use electrical energy, rather than wiring accessories or distribution equipment.
distinction: A luminaire and an independent motor are current-using equipment but are not treated as appliances by this definition.

meaning: A circuit is the group of electrical equipment supplied from one origin and protected against overcurrent by the same protective device or coordinated set of devices.
studyNote: The definition ties a circuit to both its supply origin and its overcurrent protection. That is why circuit identification, design current, conductor sizing and protective-device selection are considered together.
distinction: A final circuit directly supplies outlets or current-using equipment; a distribution circuit supplies another distribution board or switchgear.

meaning: A consumer unit is a distribution assembly, used principally in domestic premises, that brings together incoming isolation and the protective or control devices for outgoing circuits.
studyNote: For study, separate the function from the historical product wording: it receives the supply, provides a main means of isolation and distributes that supply through protective devices to final circuits.
distinction: The quoted 2015 definition uses older 'type-tested' wording. Current product requirements and assembly standards have moved on, so use the historical wording for study rather than as a current product specification.

currentGuide.note: The 2026 On-Site Guide treats consumer units and similar switchgear as assemblies selected to the relevant current assembly standard, including BS EN IEC 61439-3, and gives current enclosure and installation considerations.

meaning: Current-using equipment is equipment whose purpose is to convert electrical energy into another useful form such as light, heat or mechanical motion.
studyNote: This is a broad functional category. It helps distinguish loads from equipment whose main role is distribution, switching, protection or connection.

meaning: A distribution board receives one or more incoming circuits and distributes power to outgoing circuits through switching and protective devices, with the necessary neutral and protective-conductor terminals.
studyNote: It is a distribution and protection point rather than a load. Isolation, signalling and control may be built into the board or provided separately.
distinction: A consumer unit is a particular type of distribution board; not every distribution board is a consumer unit.

currentGuide.note: The 2026 On-Site Guide discusses current consumer-unit and distribution-board assemblies together with their protective devices and the applicable assembly standard.

meaning: A distribution circuit is a circuit whose job is to feed another distribution board, switchgear assembly, outbuilding or separate installation rather than directly supply normal points of utilization.
studyNote: It sits upstream of one or more final circuits and is often described informally as a sub-main where it feeds a remote board or separate part of an installation.
distinction: A final circuit supplies current-using equipment or outlets directly; a distribution circuit supplies another distribution point.

meaning: Electrical equipment is the broad umbrella term for items used to generate, convert, transmit, distribute, measure, protect or use electrical energy.
studyNote: The category is intentionally wide: machines, transformers, protective devices, wiring systems, accessories, appliances and luminaires can all be electrical equipment.

meaning: An electrical installation is the coordinated collection of associated electrical equipment arranged to fulfil particular purposes.
studyNote: The emphasis is on the whole coordinated installation, not on one device. Design, protection, wiring, switching, earthing and verification all relate back to this complete assembly.

meaning: An external influence is something outside the installation itself that can affect how it must be designed or how safely it can operate.
studyNote: Examples of the kind of influence designers must consider include environmental conditions, mechanical effects, the nature of the location and the people or activities present. The definition itself is deliberately broad.

meaning: A final circuit is the downstream circuit that directly supplies current-using equipment, socket-outlets or other outlet points.
studyNote: It is the last circuit in the distribution chain before the load or outlet, which is why final-circuit rules commonly address cable size, protective devices, disconnection and permissible circuit arrangements.
distinction: A distribution circuit feeds a distribution board or switchgear; a final circuit feeds utilization points.

currentGuide.note: The 2026 On-Site Guide has a dedicated final-circuits section covering standard radial, ring and lighting circuits together with protective devices, cable sizes, disconnection assumptions and maximum lengths.

meaning: Fixed equipment is equipment intended to stay secured in one defined position, either fastened to a support or otherwise fixed in place.
studyNote: Whether equipment is fixed, stationary or mobile can change which installation and protective considerations apply.
distinction: Fixed equipment is always secured in position; stationary equipment is a broader historical category that also included heavy equipment without a carrying handle.

meaning: A fused connection unit (FCU) is a fixed-wiring accessory that provides a connection point for an appliance and contains a replaceable cartridge fuse link.
studyNote: It allows the connected appliance or flexible cable to have local fuse protection as part of the fixed installation.
distinction: A fused spur is a common search name for an FCU, but 'spur' on its own is a circuit branch and is a different definition.

meaning: A low-voltage switchgear and controlgear assembly is a coordinated combination of switching devices and associated control, measurement, signalling, protection and regulating equipment, including its internal connections and structure.
studyNote: The key idea is an assembled system rather than an individual switch or breaker.
distinction: A switch, circuit-breaker or RCD can be a component within an assembly; the assembly is the complete coordinated unit.

currentGuide.note: The 2026 On-Site Guide discusses consumer units and similar low-voltage switchgear assemblies against current assembly standards and installation requirements.

meaning: A luminaire is the complete lighting equipment that distributes, filters or transforms light and includes the parts needed to support, protect and connect the light source, while the historical definition excludes the lamp itself.
studyNote: This distinguishes the complete fitting from the replaceable light source and from general appliances.

meaning: Mobile equipment is electrical equipment that is moved during operation or can readily be moved while it remains connected to the supply.
studyNote: The historical text notes 'portable equipment' as deprecated terminology. The practical point is that movement while connected is part of the intended use.
distinction: Do not equate 'mobile' with merely small: the definition is about movement in service or ease of movement while connected.

meaning: The origin of an installation is the point at which electrical energy is delivered into that installation.
studyNote: It is the reference point from which the installation begins for matters such as supply characteristics, main isolation, earthing arrangements and distribution.

meaning: A plug is an accessory with pins that engage a socket-outlet and with means to electrically connect and mechanically retain a flexible cable.
studyNote: It forms the detachable supply-side part of a plug-and-socket connection.
distinction: A connector in a cable or appliance coupler has female contacts; a plug has pins.

meaning: A point in wiring is the termination of fixed wiring provided so that current-using equipment can be connected.
studyNote: The term describes the end-use termination of the fixed wiring, not the equipment connected to it.

meaning: A socket-outlet is a fixed-wiring accessory with female contacts intended to receive a plug.
studyNote: It provides a standardized detachable connection between the fixed installation and plug-connected equipment.
distinction: The historical definition explicitly excludes a luminaire track system from being treated as a socket-outlet system.

meaning: Stationary equipment is equipment that is fixed, or—under the historical definition—has a mass over 18 kg and no carrying handle.
studyNote: The category distinguishes equipment expected to remain in place from equipment intended to be moved while connected.
distinction: This 18 kg threshold is part of the supplied 2015 definition and should not be generalized as a current rule outside that historical context.

meaning: A switchboard is an assembly of switchgear, with or without instruments, used for distribution or control; groups of local final-circuit switches are not included.
studyNote: The term refers to a coordinated board or panel, not simply several nearby switches.

meaning: Switchgear is the assembled main and auxiliary switching equipment used to operate, regulate, protect or otherwise control an electrical installation.
studyNote: It is a broad equipment category covering switching and protective functions rather than one particular device.

meaning: A wiring system is the conductors—cables or busbars—together with the parts that support, secure and, where necessary, enclose them.
studyNote: The term therefore includes more than the conductor itself: the chosen support and containment form part of the wiring system.
